examples_material_LP.differences: Translation B claims the auspicious rites occupy the 'end' of the five rites, whereas Translation A omits this specific structural claim found in the text.
Translation A identifies the final commentator as Wang Kuai, while Translation B identifies him as Wang Yan; additionally, Translation A ends mid-sentence while Translation B completes the thought.
Translation A identifies the target of instruction as 'soldiers' while Translation B correctly identifies them as 'scholars' (shi 士), and they differ on the specific name of the commentator Hu.
Translation B reverses the reading order of the page, starting from the left side and moving to the right, whereas the original text and Translation A follow the standard right-to-left columns.

Translation B includes an attribution to 'Kong' (Kong Yingda) and a different title for the work in the margin, while Translation A identifies the source as 'Essentials of the Sea of Meanings of the Zhouyi'.
Translation B correctly identifies and translates the headwords (乂, 沒, 密, 載, 再, 節, 跡, 瘵, 蔡, 察, 卒, 菜) which are largely missing or conflated in Translation A.

Translation A claims the account of Gong Liu restoring the legacy is not supported by evidence, whereas the page and Translation B state that the claims regarding his name/title lack evidence while the restoration itself is part of the narrative.
Translation A claims Mars does not have a regular path while Translation B claims it moves constantly, and they differ on whether the 180-day period involves retreating or guarding.

examples_material_PK.differences: Translation A includes a title and page number found in the margin and a concluding phrase about a 'complete collection' not present in the source text, while Translation B cuts off mid-sentence at the end of the page.
Translation B incorrectly translates 'not mentioned in the presence of others' as 'not mentioned in her presence' and misinterprets the relationship between mother and wife taboos.
Translation A misinterprets the name of the historical figure 'Tu' (突) as 'emergency' and 'Zhai Zhong Zu' (祭仲足) as 'Zhai Zhong Zuo', while Translation B correctly identifies the names and titles.
Translation B includes the final sentence of the page and the marginalia (Jin Qianshan, Section Thirteen) which Translation A omits.
Translation B includes the book title and volume number from the margin, and provides a more literal translation of the final quote from Xunzi.
Translation B includes the opening sentence regarding Zheng Xuan and the exhalations/inhalations of qi, whereas Translation A omits this and begins mid-sentence.
